- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.3) and recent prices are rising — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially <0.2) or trending downward — model fails to capture sharp declines.
- Lagged corrections: if true price drops after a forecast spike, reduce next-period forecast by 5–10% to account for momentum decay.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, adjust downward by 2–5% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overreact to short-term sentiment spikes — dampen forecast slope after 10–15 days of high sentiment.
- When sentiment is flat or mildly negative, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast by 3–5% if recent 3-day average is below 70.00.
